newsitem.title: PERU: Lima bolsa ends off as profit-taking continues.
newsitem.headline: Lima bolsa ends off as profit-taking continues.

text.p: Lima shares slipped Wednesday for the second consecutive session as profit-taking after the market's recent bull run outweighed optimism over improved economic growth figures, brokers said.
They predicted gains would return Thursday as the country's growth prospects and investor enthusiasm for mining stocks once again came to the fore.
According to preliminary figures, the bolsa's General Index lost 1.94 percent Wednesday to 2,124.87 points while the blue-chip Selective Index was off 2.34 percent to 3,057.61 points.
"The fall is a natural reaction after the strong gains achieved before the good April growth figures came out," said Bruno Calle, of Argenta brokerage.

Year-on-year gross domestic product growth was 13.4 percent in April, the highest monthly rise in more than two years. But the figure had been expected and was factored into the market in sessions preceding Tuesday's announcement.
Miner Morococha lost 4.1 percent to 5.85 soles in Wednesday's session, while Atacocha fell 0.88 percent to 2.25 soles and brewery group Union de Cervecerias Backus dipped 5.22 percent to 2.54 soles.
Benchmark Telefonica del Peru also fell 2.25 percent to 6.94 soles, but electric utilities Luz del Sur and Edelnor gained 0.94 percent and 0.92 percent to 3.23 soles and 2.20 soles respectively.
"The electricity companies are a good buy at the moment, because they have a guaranteed market and the economic growth supports their quick growth," said Percy Romero, of Fortuna brokerage.
Overall, 44 shares fell, 24 rose and 26 ended flat.
